_doc: Grand Line soundtrack manifest. Every track names its audio source (open-licence music from OpenGameArt, with composer, licence and credit) or an ElevenLabs prompt to generate it. Raw files go in tools/music/raw/<id>.mp3|wav|flac; run tools/music/prepare.py (see docs/SOUNDTRACK.md). status: planned -> review -> approved; only review/approved tracks with a prepared file play in game.
identity: Shared Grand Line motif: a hopeful rising four-note phrase (1-2-3-5 of the major scale). Islands state it in their own instruments and keys; boss themes turn it heroic or dark.
loop_rules: Every prompt asks for a steady tempo and even energy from the first bar to the last, no intro from silence, no fade-out and no final ending, so the preparer can join the end back to the start.

tracks.notes: Pirate starting village, Lv 1-10: farms, windmills, wooden houses and the first quest giver.

source.title: In Tranquil Spring
source.credit: "In Tranquil Spring" Composed by Jonathan Shaw (www.jshaw.co.uk)

tracks.elevenlabs_prompt: Warm, cheerful folk-orchestral video game exploration theme, instrumental only. Fingerpicked acoustic guitar and a wooden flute carry a simple, singable major-key melody built on a hopeful rising four-note phrase, supported by light pizzicato and legato strings, soft hand percussion and gentle shaker at a relaxed walking tempo around 96 BPM. Innocent, sunny and optimistic, like the first morning of a grand sea adventure. The arrangement grows gently from guitar and flute to fuller strings in the middle, then settles back to the opening texture, keeping a steady tempo and even energy throughout with no fade-out and no big ending, so it loops seamlessly. Crisp, natural, warm acoustic production, no vocals.

tracks.notes: Marine starting island, Lv 1-10: white fortress with three domed towers, gates, courtyard and a timber-framed town with an octagon plaza.

tracks.elevenlabs_prompt: Optimistic orchestral naval academy theme for a video game, instrumental only. Crisp military snare drum cadence, warm French horns and trumpets stating a hopeful rising four-note fanfare motif, clarinet and flute countermelodies, and uplifting legato strings at a brisk, proud marching tempo around 108 BPM in a bright major key. Disciplined, ambitious and full of camaraderie, like young recruits starting a naval career, but light enough for long exploration rather than a battle. Even energy from start to end with no fade-out and no final cadence so it loops seamlessly. Clean, natural orchestral production, no vocals.
